LoadState under -race; (2) offline client reconnects to a different hub, gets missed ops, offline ops applied and acked exactly once; (3) a killed hub's clients reconnect elsewhere with no lost or duplicated op; (4) cursor hub A to hub B < 200ms, AwarenessSync on join, removal on leave and TTL expiry; (5) Phase 1 tests still pass
why: falsifiable runs taken from brief Phase 2 acceptance, service 03/04 descriptions and presence latency target

decision: rigor high; architect arena with three model families before code; each unit verified on the real multi-process stack, then committed and pushed to main
why: the cross-instance ordering and replay contract is a one-way door; user asked for chunked pushes to main per phase

decision: add Redis 7 to docker-compose on 56379 and COLLAB_TEST_REDIS_URL to make test-integration
why: every candidate design needs Redis for doc:{id} fan-out and presence TTL keys; design-independent so it lands first
evidence: docker compose up --wait: redis Healthy, PONG

decision: Opus design is the base: strict seq-ordered delivery, resume by one seq, catch-up-on-join keeps the clock bound
why: One resume number is exact only if delivery is seq-ordered; catch-up makes every honest dependency present before validation

decision: Drop the 8k replay ring; MissedOps always reads document-service
why: Laziness: a second copy of the log with no measured need

decision: Hub keeps single-instance mode with in-process bus and loopback presence when Redis/presence unset
why: Phase 1 suite and local dev stay independent of new services (Grok)

decision: Newest connection wins per hub for a client ID
why: Auto-reconnect to the same hub while the old socket is half-open must not be rejected (Grok)

decision: Reject Grok per-client clock==vector+1 and GPT bound removal
why: Lamport clocks jump past others' ops; removal reopens clock exhaustion

decision: Presence expiry by deadline zset sweep, not keyspace notifications
why: Notifications are lossy, lazy, and need server config; sweep is deterministic for TTL tests

decision: Units: 1 docsvc seqs, 2 single-hub seq stream, 3 client resume, 4 Redis fanout, 5 N-hub runs 1-3, 6 presence-service (parallel), 7 hub presence run 4
why: Each unit ends in a check and is pushed to main on its own

decision: AppendOperations returns per-op seqs and first_new_seq; ReadOperations range read
why: Hubs need seqs for ordered delivery and duplicate acks; first_new_seq is required because existing ops at the old op_seq are adjacent to the new range
evidence: store+grpc tests on real Postgres under -race

decision: presence-service: Lua is the only writer, publishes events in-script, deadline zset sweep
why: Atomic state change plus event; sweep picks one winner via ZREM
evidence: store/grpc tests on real Redis -race x2

decision: Client IDs pass to Lua as varint bytes; expiry member doc|decimal|varintHex; Apply validates whole batch first
why: Lua numbers are doubles and corrupt uint64 above 2^53; partial apply on invalid batch

decision: Hub delivers strictly seq-ordered frames via fanout.Sequencer; gap fill from ReadOperations after 30ms grace; DocumentSync only at G empty; newest connection wins
why: One resume number is exact; the fan-out and resume units only plug into the Sequencer
evidence: full race suite incl. e2e/load; new hub tests x50; three mutation checks failed the right tests

decision: Empty fill with open gap counts as failure; undeliverable sequenced op fail-stops CODE_INTERNAL
why: An open gap implies the log holds D+1, so an empty read means a broken log; a log that will not apply is a server bug

decision: Resume by seq: catch-up to the client's seq before validation, MissedOps within 20k else DocumentSync; collabclient offline buffer, ack-by-stream, auto-reconnect
why: Exactly-once across reconnect: the log dedupes resends and the stream acks them
evidence: 30x new tests, full suite x2, mutations on catch-up and MissedOps ack caught

decision: Every MissedOps frame carries seq D
why: Client must know when the last frame arrived before resending

decision: CODE_UNAVAILABLE is the only retryable code; other codes close and are terminal; invalid cursors dropped silently; load failure is UNAVAILABLE
why: Auto-reconnect looped forever on rejected ops; cursor races sent non-closing errors

decision: Redis Pub/Sub fan-out: publish FirstNewSeq..OpSeq after Append; deliver via Sequencer; heal by gap, 1s idle poll, resubscribe resync; fanout.Memory when REDIS_URL unset
why: Redis is a latency hint; Postgres seq stays the only order; Redis loss never fail-stops
evidence: full suite; new tests x30; six mutations each caught by their target test

decision: Defer Redis subscriber health ping to the presence unit
why: Ops heal via 1s idle poll on a half-open subscriber; presence events would not, so the ping lands with presence
